finding.text: The local-dev design docs still describe the deleted setup: `public/imagine/platform/decisions/local-dev.md:22,35,39,60,90` names `wrangler.dev.jsonc` and `worker/schema.sql`, and `dev.mjs:3` still points readers at "local-dev.md" for how the two servers work. Point them at `worker/wrangler.jsonc`, `worker/migrations/` and `worker/seed/dev.sql`, or add a "superseded by worker/readme.md" line at the top.

Other stale names for the same files: `public/imagine/platform/decisions/identity.md:64` (`wrangler.dev.jsonc`), `public/imagine/cms/d1/doc/decisions.md:12-13,83` (`worker/schema.sql`, `worker/seed.sql`, `wrangler.dev.jsonc`), `public/imagine/platform/readme.md:47` and `public/imagine/platform/decisions/slice.md:57` (`worker/seed.sql`), and `public/imagine/platform/local/page.js:69,87`. Add a one-line "now: …" pointer to each. Don't rewrite the history.

`worker/readme.md` no longer says outright that real Google sign-in is untested. The old `app/readme.md:49` did. Every stage has `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ""` (`worker/wrangler.jsonc:26,39,48`), so "staging verified end to end" covers only flows that use minted cookies, and Google login has never run. One line under "What the owner must do" would make that plain.

Bans exist only in the dev login: `worker/dev.js:24` puts a `banned` flag in the cookie, and nothing on staging or production can set it (no KV, no column). So a real user can't be banned yet. The `can.js:2` comment reads as if bans work. It's worth one line in the readme's "not built" list.

`ADMIN_GOOGLE_SUB`, which the old `app/readme.md:31` supported, was dropped. Only `ADMIN_EMAIL` is left (`worker/index.js:41`). That's fine, because `google.js` now requires `email_verified`. It's recorded here only because the readme doesn't mention the drop.

Once this merges and reaches `main`, the assets-only root Worker will serve `public/app/` on lew42.com with no API behind it. `/api/config` falls back to the single-page `index.html`, and `public/app/app.js:8` turns that into `{}`. The result is a login page that can't sign anyone in, plus a service worker registered on lew42.com. Strictly, that changes what lew42.com serves before the cutover. A "this host has no API" message in `app.js` would make it harmless.

`DocStore` moved into `public/framework/core/Item/DocStore.js` without the lean core test that rule 12 asks for (`DocStore.test.mjs`). The new classes `Room` and `UserDO` have no page showing their live instances. The admin users list covers users, but nothing lists open rooms or documents with their lock holders.

`deploy.mjs` deploys (`worker/scripts/deploy.mjs:26`) before it creates `SESSION_SECRET` (`:28-36`). On a first deploy there is a short window where every sign-in returns 500. Production's first deploy is still to come, so swap the order or say so in the cutover steps.

The local-dev design docs still describe the deleted setup. `public/imagine/platform/decisions/local-dev.md:22,35,39,60,90` names `wrangler.dev.jsonc` and `worker/schema.sql`, and `dev.mjs:2` sends readers to "local-dev.md" to learn how the two servers work. Add a "now: worker/wrangler.jsonc, worker/migrations/, worker/seed/dev.sql; see worker/readme.md" line at the top of local-dev.md. Don't rewrite its history.

Other docs still name the deleted files: `public/imagine/platform/decisions/identity.md:64` (`wrangler.dev.jsonc`), `public/imagine/cms/d1/doc/decisions.md:12-13,83` (`worker/schema.sql`, `worker/seed.sql`, `wrangler.dev.jsonc`), `public/imagine/platform/readme.md:47`, `public/imagine/platform/decisions/slice.md:57` and `public/imagine/platform/local/page.js:69,87`. Each needs a one-line pointer to the new name. I re-ran `git grep` on the worktree and all of these still hit.

The R2 bucket name for production disagrees between files. `worker/readme.md` ("What the owner must do", step 4) says to create `monorepo-docs`, but the `worker/wrangler.jsonc:19-20` comment says `monorepo-<stage>-docs`, which makes it `monorepo-production-docs`. Pick one name, because the owner will follow the readme step by hand.

The readme doesn't say that real Google sign-in has never run. `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is `""` on every stage (`worker/wrangler.jsonc:24,37,47`), so "staging verified" covers only flows with minted cookies. `google.js:21` rejects every token until the owner finishes steps 1 and 2. One sentence under "What the owner must do" would make that plain.

A ban only works in the dev login. `resolveUser` reads `banned` from the cookie payload (`worker/index.js:29`), and only `worker/dev.js` puts it there. There is no column and no admin route, so a real user on staging or production can't be banned. `can.js:2-3` reads as if bans work. Add it to a "not built yet" line in the readme.

After this merges and reaches `main`, the assets-only root Worker serves `public/app/` on lew42.com with no API behind it. `/api/config` falls back to the SPA `index.html`, and `public/app/app.js:8` turns that into `{}`. The result is a login page that can't sign in, and it registers a service worker on lew42.com before the announced cutover. A "this host has no API" message when `/api/config` isn't JSON would make it harmless.

`deploy.mjs` deploys (`worker/scripts/deploy.mjs:26`) before it creates `SESSION_SECRET` (`:28-36`). On production's first deploy, sign-in returns 500 for a short window (`index.js:58`). Move the secret step before `deploy`. That works because `wrangler secret put` creates the Worker if it doesn't exist.

The rule asks for one lean core test per class, but `DocStore` moved into `public/framework/core/Item/DocStore.js` without a `DocStore.test.mjs`. `Room` and `UserDO` hold live state, but no page shows their instances: nothing lists open documents with their lock holders.

`worker/readme.md` ("Production cutover", step 1) says "My API token cannot…", which is an agent's first person in a readme. "The agents' Cloudflare token cannot…" says the same thing in the readme's own voice.

The site's own entry `public/app.js` and the new folder `public/app/` (with its own `app.js`) now sit side by side. Many docs cite `public/app.js` (for example `public/framework/dev/DevBar/doc/decisions.md:24`), so a reader can confuse the two. It isn't broken, but `public/app/readme.md` could say in one line that it isn't the site's `app.js`.

`worker/readme.md` is out of date: its "Not built yet" list still says "A page that lists live documents and their lock holders, **and a `DocStore` test**". That test now exists (`public/framework/core/Item/DocStore.test.mjs`, and I ran it: PASS, 9 checks). Drop the words "and a `DocStore` test" so a fresh agent doesn't write it a second time.

`public/imagine/platform/decisions/identity.md:64` now says `dev.js` is "imported only by the `main` of `worker/wrangler.jsonc`", and the next line calls `worker/index.js` "the production `main`". Both are a `main` of that same file now, so the sentence reads as if it contradicts itself. "the `main` of `worker/wrangler.jsonc`'s local stage" would say it exactly.

There is still no page that shows the live `Room` and `UserDO` instances (which documents are open, and who holds each lock). The readme records it under "Not built yet", and this diff doesn't touch it.

`/imagine/platform/local/` is 57% empty at 3440 (layout.json `empty 0.568`, ink 0.441). The page's columns stay at prose width and leave the right side empty. This was already true before the diff, which only changed one sentence of text on the page.
